verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Data from Table 4 (page 6), text-extracted (machine-readable PDF, not scanned).

notes: Source: Bhargava et al., Front. Microbiol. 2022;13:965053 (Hayes Memorial Mission Hospital, Prayagraj UP). Table 4 reports % susceptible (confirmed by Results text, e.g. 'amikacin was effective against 77.0% of E. coli'; 'imipenem outperformed meropenem by inhibiting 57.4% E. coli'). All values entered as printed %S; no %R conversion needed (from_R=false throughout). NT = not tested (cell omitted). Specimen = clean-catch midstream urine; study period Nov 2018-Dec 2019; 96.0% of isolates MDR. ESBL context: 40.4% of E. coli were ESBL producers; none of K. pneumoniae were ESBL. n per organism from Table 4 column headers. Proteus sp. is filed under the genus (species not stated). Enterococcus not split to species → 'Enterococcus'. 'H-gentamycin' (high-concentration gentamicin, Enterococcus 66.7%) recorded as separate token h-gentamicin. Non-canonical drugs kept with lowercase tokens: novobiocin. S. epidermidis (n=8) reported but not in canonical organism list, see unmapped. No A. baumannii in study.
issues: Organism naming over-specification: the extraction labels the second organism 'Proteus mirabilis', but Table 4 and the text report only 'Proteus sp.' (species not identified). All 14 susceptibility values map correctly to the Proteus column; only the top-level name is over-specified. The extraction includes a note acknowledging this, but the displayed name 'Proteus mirabilis' is not supported by t

No %R->%S conversion issues found: Table 4 prints susceptibility (%S) directly (confirmed by narrative on p5, e.g. vancomycin 100% S. aureus, nitrofurantoin 94.4% Enterococcus, chloramphenicol 83.3/75.0/87.5). All from_R:false flags are correct.

S. aureus clindamycin s:55.0 is ambiguous in the source (only two values, 55.0% and 62.5%, appear in the clindamycin row across the three gram-positive columns).
